assumptions.summary: All collected data are treated as accurate despite acknowledged measurement and context errors.
Every rider begins fully restored at Pmax0 and E0.
Experienced riders always choose the most suitable gear, absorbed into a conversion coefficient.
No illness, fall, injury, or unexpected incident occurs.
Wind, humidity, and other environmental parameters remain constant during a race.
Male and female comparison scenarios use the same number of laps.
Team riders are point objects rotating through fixed position drag percentages.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Maximum-effort experiments from cited literature are used to rectify six rider parameters, but raw observations are not packaged.
Table 1 supplies TTS/sprinter male/female values for kf, kr, kin, kout, Pmax0, and E0.
Tokyo, Flanders, and a designed course are sampled from Google Earth and reconstructed in local 3D coordinates.
Road records retain segment length, height difference, inclination, and curvature radius.
A typical mechanics table fixes mass 60 kg, efficiency 0.99, area 0.35 m2, Cd 0.05, density 1.1 kg/m3, and mu 0.003.
The implemented DP grid reports nx=400, nv=30, np=10, ne=10, nr=450 and about ten minutes on a 2020 M1 MacBook Pro.
Weather results use one TTS male under ideal, rainy, and headwind scenarios.
Team drag multipliers are 100, 63, 58, 56, 55, and 54 percent of the leading rider's drag.

models.summary: Eq.1-Eq.3 combine power-dependent fatigue with exponential recovery toward Pmax0.
Eq.4-Eq.6 define Pin, Pout, and the integrated reserve E.
Algorithm 1 sweeps trial power, updates Pmax/E, stops at a boundary, and plots duration versus power.
The road interface stores x/y/z coordinates, Eq.7 length/height/slope, and a three-point circumcircle radius.
Eq.8 balances power-derived thrust, aerodynamic drag, rolling/slope forces, and braking; the curve interface caps speed by static friction.
Eq.9 defines the constrained minimum-time problem, Eq.10 the state transfer, and Eq.11 the Bellman recurrence.
Eq.12 supplies a scalar wind-speed modification and humidity changes mu for scenario simulations.
Eq.13 adds a normally distributed error process to the target power trajectory.
The team extension uses 100/63/58/56/55/54 percent drag positions and periodic leader-to-tail rotation.

weaknesses.summary: Assuming all heterogeneous collected data are accurate contradicts the paper's own acknowledgement of measurement and contextual error.
The gear-assumption explanation appears mechanically reversed and removes gear selection without validating a constant efficiency.
kf and kr are printed with unit 1 although Eq.1-Eq.3 require inverse-time dimensions.
E is stored in joules but interpreted as blood-glucose concentration; no biochemical conversion or glycogen limit is supplied.
Eq.4 makes energy replenishment proportional to muscle fatigue without direct calibration, and kin is printed dimensionless.
The six-parameter rectification omits raw maximum-effort observations, objective, optimization method, residuals, and uncertainty.
Algorithm 1 omits dt, integration method, power-step details, initialization safeguards, and curve-convergence checks.
The profile results contain no quantitative fit metric or held-out athlete validation.
Google Earth sampling is manual/qualitative, with no coordinates, projection method, sampling threshold, or reconstruction error.
Three-point circumcircle curvature is noise-sensitive and endpoint/collinear cases are not fully specified.
Eq.8 divides power by v and is singular at the zero-speed initial state; wheel inertia and drivetrain dynamics are omitted.
The same mu concept is used for rolling resistance and maximum static curve friction without a separate tire/road model.
Eq.10 uses Delta t=(xi-xj)/vj and vi=vj+a Delta t, which is inconsistent with constant-acceleration distance unless acceleration is negligible.
Eq.10's energy transition subtracts Prider Delta t but omits kout and uses a k_i symbol inconsistent with kin.
Eq.11 uses max to update a value defined as minimum cumulative time, reversing the Bellman optimization direction.
The DP reports complexity and runtime but no grid-convergence, feasibility residual, memory, code, or path-reconstruction check.
The claim that gender makes no significant strategy difference is based on plotted curves without a statistical test.
Figure 15's expected uphill/downhill pattern is internal physical consistency, not external validation.
Eq.12 computes scalar relative speed as an absolute sum/difference times cos(theta), rather than vector relative velocity before drag.
The text says wet ground reduces speed but also says mu is smaller for higher humidity and larger for dry ground, conflicting with rolling/static friction roles.
Rain/headwind times omit exact humidity, wind direction/speed, coefficient changes, and route/rider parameter bundle.
Eq.13 specifies only a normal marginal error; variance, correlation, clipping, seed, replicates, and confidence intervals are absent.
The disturbed finish time is one realization and cannot establish sensitivity or robustness.
The team simulation omits rider-specific fatigue states, handover dynamics, spacing/yaw, interval search grid, and fourth-rider finish rule.
The claimed best replacement interval and 22:36 team time cannot be reproduced from the paper.
The memo describes a usable tool and parameter-calculation workflow, but no executable tool, data package, or user validation is included.
Memo advice for climbers, puncheurs, and rouleurs extends beyond the two modeled rider types.
Extracted text contains encoding corruption; rendered 200-DPI pages are authoritative for formulas and typography.
Eq.10 writes the next Pmax state as fatigue and recovery increments without adding the predecessor Pmax,j, so it computes an increment rather than a successor state.
Algorithm 1 resets E for each trial power but does not visibly reset Pmax to Pmax0, allowing one constant-power experiment to contaminate the next.
Algorithm 1 may leave t unset when the inner loop reaches its hard i<800 limit without a break, and the treatment of censored durations is not stated.
Pmax0 is defined in watts in the notation table but labeled in joules in Table 1 and Algorithm 1 inputs.
Eq.8 uses k_rider while the notation and typical-parameter table define k_wheel; their equivalence is not declared.
The Summary gives dry/tailwind and gender-significance conclusions without a corresponding dry/tailwind result panel or statistical significance test.
Several result plots omit clear axis names or units, the memo breaks many words mid-token, and Sprinter recommendations differ between uphill, large-uphill, and end/short-climb emphases.
